intervention_label: Doxorubicin + trabectedin induction, then trabectedin maintenance (LMS-04)
access_summary: Both drugs are stocked at any sarcoma infusion center, so delivery is not the problem. The problem is the label: Yondelis is approved for leiomyosarcoma only after a prior anthracycline-containing regimen, and she is anthracycline-naive, so the planned first-line pairing is off-label prescribing carried by the LMS-04 phase 3 result. Build the prior authorization as an off-label first-line request from the outset rather than filing it and waiting for the denial.
regulatory_status: Doxorubicin: FDA-approved, generic. Trabectedin (Yondelis): FDA-approved 2015 for unresectable or metastatic liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma after a prior anthracycline-containing regimen. The first-line combination sits outside that label.
guideline_status: Doxorubicin-based first-line therapy is standard in NCCN soft tissue sarcoma; the specific doxorubicin + trabectedin pairing follows LMS-04. Category not independently verified this run.

trials.title: Doxorubicin with trabectedin then trabectedin maintenance versus doxorubicin alone (LMS-04)
trials.notes: The pivotal trial behind the planned regimen. Closed; listed as the evidence anchor for the payer file, not as an enrollment option. Note it capped performance status at ECOG 0-1, which her chart does not document.

manufacturer.company: Janssen Products, LP (Johnson & Johnson); trabectedin originator PharmaMar
manufacturer.notes: Phone taken verbatim from the current FDA label: 'For more information, call 1-800-526-7736 or go to www.YONDELIS.com'.

payer_access_notes: Doxorubicin is generic and uncontested. Trabectedin is the expensive component and the label's prior-anthracycline requirement is the hook a payer will pull on. Cite the LMS-04 primary report and the final overall survival analysis plus whatever compendium listing the treating pharmacy can pull. Sarcoma centers win this appeal routinely, but only when it is filed as an off-label first-line request.
next_steps: Document an ECOG score at the next clinic visit. It is undocumented, it gates most of the trial options in this dossier, and it costs nothing.
Get the baseline echocardiogram with LVEF, hepatic and renal panels, CBC read against altitude-adjusted haemoglobin references, and PFTs with DLCO and resting oximetry measured at her home altitude.
File the trabectedin prior authorization as an off-label first-line request citing LMS-04, before cycle 1 rather than after a denial.
Arrange central venous access; trabectedin runs as a 24-hour infusion.
For label or coverage questions call Janssen medical information at 1-800-526-7736.
geographic_scope: US-wide; any sarcoma-capable infusion center
notes: Starting this regimen is the event that closes the first-line window. Several trials in this dossier admit only treatment-naive or one-prior-line patients, and a few close permanently once cumulative doxorubicin accumulates. Sequence the diagnostics and the trial outreach before cycle 1, not after.

access_summary: Two generics, stocked everywhere, given in uLMS as long-standing off-label practice that payers do not fight. It is the first-line fallback if the baseline LVEF or her pulmonary reserve at 8,500 ft rules out full-dose doxorubicin. There is also a first-line-eligible randomised trial built on this backbone at MD Anderson (see the abemaciclib row), which is worth a call before committing to the regimen off-protocol.
regulatory_status: Both FDA-approved for other indications and available as generics; neither carries a sarcoma indication.
guideline_status: Long-established NCCN soft tissue sarcoma option for LMS

trials.title: Abemaciclib added to gemcitabine and docetaxel for soft tissue sarcoma
trials.notes: Phase 2 explicitly states patients may be systemic-treatment naive, and ECOG ceiling is 2 rather than 1. Prior gemcitabine is not allowed in phase 2, so this closes if she receives gemcitabine off-protocol first. Single site: MD Anderson, Houston.

payer_access_notes: Generic pricing keeps prior-authorization friction near zero; compendium support for sarcoma use is old and settled.
next_steps: Hold as the backup plan pending the LVEF and PFT results that gate doxorubicin.
Before giving gemcitabine off-protocol, call MD Anderson at 866-632-6789 about NCT06498648, which requires gemcitabine-naive status in its phase 2 portion.
If used off-protocol, plan G-CSF support per the GOG dosing experience.
geographic_scope: US-wide

access_summary: Both agents are generic and available at any sarcoma center; the combination is standard practice supported by EORTC 62012 even though neither label names uterine leiomyosarcoma. Nothing blocks access. The reasons to prefer or avoid it are toxicity and the mesna/hydration burden, not availability.
regulatory_status: Both FDA-approved, generic; no uterine leiomyosarcoma indication on either label.
guideline_status: NCCN soft tissue sarcoma first-line option where a higher response rate is the goal
payer_access_notes: Generic; no meaningful coverage barrier.
next_steps: Same baseline cardiac and pulmonary workup as any anthracycline plan.
If considered, weigh against the cumulative-doxorubicin ceiling that also gates the in vivo lung perfusion trial.
geographic_scope: US-wide

access_summary: Yondelis names leiomyosarcoma on its label, but only after a prior anthracycline-containing regimen. Today she is anthracycline-naive, so single-agent use would be off-label; after LMS-04 induction it becomes on-label, at which point she will already have had it. The practical read is that trabectedin is fully available to her, and the label question is about line, not about the drug.
regulatory_status: FDA-approved (Yondelis, 2015) for unresectable or metastatic liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma after a prior anthracycline-containing regimen.
guideline_status: NCCN soft tissue sarcoma option for LMS after anthracycline

trials.title: Trabectedin in metastatic or locally advanced leiomyosarcoma (Italian Sarcoma Group)
trials.indication: unresectable or metastatic leiomyosarcoma after anthracycline
trials.notes: Italy-only, 17 sites, and it requires prior anthracycline-based chemotherapy plus no prior trabectedin. She fails both today, and after LMS-04 she fails the no-prior-trabectedin criterion. Listed so the reader can see it was checked and closed.

payer_access_notes: On-label after an anthracycline; the appeal work all sits in the first-line combination request, not here.
next_steps: No separate access action beyond the LMS-04 prior authorization already described.
If the plan changes to single-agent trabectedin first line, the same off-label filing applies.
geographic_scope: US-wide

access_summary: Generic pair, orderable anywhere, off-label in sarcoma but supported by a randomised Spanish GEIS phase 2. Access is a non-issue; this sits in the later-line queue behind the anthracycline and gemcitabine/docetaxel options.
regulatory_status: Both FDA-approved, generic; no sarcoma indication on either label.
payer_access_notes: Generic; no barrier.
next_steps: No action now. Revisit at progression.
geographic_scope: US-wide

access_summary: Oral generic, easy to get, off-label in sarcoma. Its real relevance in this case is as the partner in the olaparib combination, where the PARP inhibitor rather than temozolomide is the cost and coverage problem.
regulatory_status: FDA-approved for glioma indications; generic. No sarcoma indication.

manufacturer.company: Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC (Temodar brand); multiple generic manufacturers
manufacturer.notes: Phone from the current Temodar FDA label.

payer_access_notes: Generic oral; low friction. Pair the request with the olaparib filing so both are reviewed together.
next_steps: Treat as an add-on to the olaparib decision rather than a separate access question.
geographic_scope: US-wide

access_summary: Halaven is approved in liposarcoma after an anthracycline, not in leiomyosarcoma, and the phase 3 that supported it found the benefit sat in the liposarcoma subgroup. So use here is off-label on a weak histology rationale. Available at any infusion center once a payer clears it, which is the whole obstacle.
regulatory_status: FDA-approved for unresectable or metastatic liposarcoma after a prior anthracycline-containing regimen, and for metastatic breast cancer. Not approved for leiomyosarcoma.
guideline_status: Listed in NCCN soft tissue sarcoma; the leiomyosarcoma evidence is weaker than the liposarcoma evidence

trials.title: Eribulin versus dacarbazine in advanced liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma
trials.indication: advanced soft tissue sarcoma after anthracycline
trials.notes: Closed. Cited because the leiomyosarcoma subgroup did not carry the survival benefit, which is what a payer reviewer will find if they read past the abstract.

manufacturer.notes: Phone from the current Halaven FDA label.

payer_access_notes: Expect an off-label denial on first pass given the liposarcoma-restricted label and the negative leiomyosarcoma subgroup. Worth pursuing only after the better-supported options are exhausted.
next_steps: Defer. Revisit after anthracycline and gemcitabine-based lines.
If pursued, call Eisai medical information at 1-877-873-4724 for the label and subgroup data before filing.
geographic_scope: US-wide

access_summary: Votrient is approved for advanced soft tissue sarcoma in patients who have had prior chemotherapy, which covers uterine leiomyosarcoma by histology but not her line: she has had no systemic therapy. It becomes on-label the moment induction is behind her. One consequence worth noting now is that taking pazopanib would disqualify her from the ivonescimab trial, which excludes prior VEGF-pathway inhibitors.
regulatory_status: FDA-approved for advanced soft tissue sarcoma in patients who have received prior chemotherapy.
guideline_status: NCCN soft tissue sarcoma option after prior chemotherapy

trials.title: Pazopanib versus placebo in soft tissue sarcoma after prior therapy (PALETTE)
trials.indication: advanced soft tissue sarcoma after prior chemotherapy
trials.notes: Closed. The registration trial; listed as the label's evidence base.

manufacturer.country_of_origin: Switzerland; US operations East Hanover, NJ
manufacturer.notes: Phone from the current Votrient FDA label.

payer_access_notes: Straightforward once a prior chemotherapy line is documented. Hepatotoxicity monitoring is a label requirement, not a coverage one.
next_steps: Hold until after a chemotherapy line; the label's prior-chemotherapy requirement is the only gate.
Before starting any VEGF-pathway drug, decide about NCT07516925 (ivonescimab), which excludes patients with prior VEGF inhibitor exposure.
geographic_scope: US-wide

access_summary: The trial that would have fit her almost perfectly, SaLuDo, is a first-line anthracycline-naive leiomyosarcoma study and it has stopped enrolling. Lurbinectedin itself is FDA-approved in small cell lung cancer, so an off-label request is technically possible, but with the phase 3 read-out not yet public there is no compendium support to hang a payer appeal on. Practically this is not a route for her right now.
regulatory_status: Lurbinectedin (Zepzelca) FDA-approved for metastatic small cell lung cancer. No sarcoma indication.

trials.title: Lurbinectedin plus doxorubicin versus doxorubicin alone, first-line metastatic leiomyosarcoma (SaLuDo)
trials.notes: Closed to accrual. Criteria otherwise matched her closely: no prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease, no prior anthracycline, ECOG 0-1. This is the single clearest example in the dossier of a trial whose title suggests a fit but whose enrolment window has already shut. 97 sites, many US.

manufacturer.notes: Phone from the current Zepzelca FDA label.

payer_access_notes: Off-label in sarcoma with no compendium listing and no published phase 3; expect denial. Revisit if SaLuDo reports positive and a listing follows.
next_steps: Confirm with the SaLuDo sites that accrual is truly closed rather than paused before writing it off; the registry status is 'active, not recruiting'.
Call Jazz medical information at 1-800-520-5568 to ask whether any expanded-access or continued-access provision exists for the sarcoma program.
Otherwise treat as unavailable in the first-line window.
geographic_scope: US and EU sites, all closed to new enrolment

access_summary: Doxil is FDA-approved in ovarian cancer, myeloma and Kaposi sarcoma, so off-label maintenance use in soft tissue sarcoma is prescribable in the US, though without guideline backing. The trial testing exactly this question (MELODY) is Taiwan-only. Either way this is a post-induction question, not a first-line one.
regulatory_status: FDA-approved (Doxil) for ovarian cancer after platinum, AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma, and multiple myeloma. No soft tissue sarcoma indication.

trials.title: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin versus active surveillance after standard anthracycline-based treatment (MELODY)
trials.indication: advanced soft tissue sarcoma with controlled disease after anthracycline
trials.notes: Seven sites, all in Taiwan. Requires completed standard anthracycline-based treatment with disease control, so it is structurally a post-induction question for her, and the geography rules it out regardless.

manufacturer.company: Baxter Healthcare Corporation (Doxil); generic PLD also marketed
manufacturer.notes: Phone from the current Doxil FDA label.

payer_access_notes: Off-label maintenance in sarcoma has no compendium listing; a payer will ask what the anthracycline maintenance evidence is, and the honest answer today is a Taiwanese phase 2 still enrolling.
next_steps: Park until the maintenance phase of LMS-04 is underway and the question is live.
If pursued then, note the cumulative doxorubicin ceiling already consumed by induction.
geographic_scope: Off-label US-wide; the MELODY trial is Taiwan-only

access_summary: This is the one trial in the dossier whose line requirement is softer than the trial table suggests: the phase 2 portion states patients may be systemic-treatment naive, and its ECOG ceiling is 2 rather than 1. It runs at a single site, MD Anderson in Houston, and prior gemcitabine is disqualifying in phase 2, so giving gemcitabine/docetaxel off-protocol first would close it. Abemaciclib is FDA-approved in breast cancer, so an off-label route exists, but with no sarcoma data outside this study a payer will not fund it.
regulatory_status: Abemaciclib (Verzenio) FDA-approved in HR-positive HER2-negative breast cancer. No sarcoma indication. Gemcitabine and docetaxel are generic.

trials.title: Testing the addition of abemaciclib to gemcitabine for soft tissue sarcoma
trials.notes: Registry text: 'Phase 2: Patients must have advanced/metastatic pathologically confirmed leiomyosarcoma or dedifferentiated liposarcoma for which gemcitabine and docetaxel is considered standard-of-care, patients may be systemic-treatment naive. Prior gemcitabine is not allowed.' ECOG ceiling is 2 (Karnofsky >= 60). Principal investigator Elise F. Nassif. One site, Houston TX.

manufacturer.notes: Phone from the current Verzenio FDA label (1-800-LillyRx).

payer_access_notes: On trial the study drug is supplied; the chemotherapy backbone bills as usual care. Off-protocol abemaciclib in sarcoma has no compendium support and will be denied.
next_steps: Call MD Anderson at 866-632-6789 about NCT06498648 phase 2 and ask directly whether the treatment-naive stratum is currently open and whether an ECOG of 2 would still screen.
Do this before starting any gemcitabine-containing regimen, since prior gemcitabine disqualifies.
Document the ECOG at the same visit; the criterion is a measured score, not an assumed one.
Plan for travel to Houston and ask the site about screening turnaround relative to the LMS-04 start date.
geographic_scope: United States; single site, MD Anderson, Houston TX
notes: Reachable before LMS-04 starts. That distinguishes it from almost every other experimental option in this dossier.

access_summary: Both drugs are approved and prescribable, and the uterine leiomyosarcoma phase 2 that generated the signal reported a real response rate, but both trials of this combination are now closed to accrual. So the only live route is an off-label prescription, and that request will go much better with a tissue HRD or HRR result in hand than with the current plasma panel, which does not settle homologous recombination status.
regulatory_status: Olaparib (Lynparza) FDA-approved in BRCA-mutated ovarian, breast, pancreatic and prostate cancers. Temozolomide approved in glioma. Neither is approved in sarcoma.

trials.title: Olaparib and temozolomide for advanced uterine leiomyosarcoma
trials.notes: Closed to accrual. 15 US sites. This is the study that produced the uLMS response signal.

trials.title: Olaparib and temozolomide versus usual treatment for uterine leiomyosarcoma after chemotherapy
trials.notes: Closed to accrual, 145 US and Puerto Rico sites. Would have been the natural post-induction landing spot. Worth one confirmatory call to the NCI trial referral line in case a site reopens.

manufacturer.country_of_origin: United Kingdom; US operations Wilmington, DE
manufacturer.notes: Phone from the current Lynparza FDA label.

payer_access_notes: Olaparib off-label in sarcoma is a hard sell without a documented HRR alteration or HRD score. A somatic BRCA1/2 or high genomic-instability result on tissue changes the conversation entirely, which is one more reason tissue order A should go out now rather than after induction.
next_steps: Send tissue order A (DNA plus RNA comprehensive profiling with an HRD or genomic-instability score) before anything else; it is the gate on this whole branch.
Order the germline homologous-recombination panel alongside rather than reflexively after a somatic finding.
Re-check NCT05432791 site status at progression; a 145-site cooperative-group study can reopen.
If pursuing off-label, call AstraZeneca medical information at 1-800-236-9933 and build the file around the tissue HRD result plus the NCI 10250 uLMS data.
geographic_scope: Off-label US-wide; both trials closed to enrolment
notes: Post-induction option. Nothing here is reachable in the first-line window except the tissue testing that gates it.

intervention_label: PARP inhibition in BRCA2-altered uterine leiomyosarcoma
access_summary: Same access mechanics as the olaparib combination row: the drug is prescribable, the histology is not on any label, and the whole question turns on whether a tissue HRR alteration exists. The plasma panel reported no BRCA1/2 alteration, but plasma negatives at low tumor fraction do not close this.
regulatory_status: PARP inhibitors approved across BRCA-mutated ovarian, breast, pancreatic and prostate cancers. No sarcoma indication.
payer_access_notes: A documented somatic or germline BRCA2 alteration is the difference between a fundable request and a reflex denial.
next_steps: Order tissue HRR sequencing with a genomic-instability score as part of tissue order A.
Add the germline homologous-recombination panel in parallel.
Only pursue a payer request once a tissue result exists.
geographic_scope: US-wide, contingent on a tissue HRR result

access_summary: Keytruda carries tumour-agnostic approvals for microsatellite-instability-high and TMB-high solid tumours, so if tissue testing returns either, she is on-label rather than off-label and coverage follows. Neither has been measured; the plasma panel did not report TMB or MSI. Without one of those results, use in leiomyosarcoma is off-label against a negative SARC028 LMS cohort, which payers know.
regulatory_status: FDA-approved across many tumour types, including tumour-agnostic indications for MSI-high/dMMR and for TMB-high (>= 10 mut/Mb) solid tumours after prior therapy. No sarcoma-specific indication.
guideline_status: Tumour-agnostic NCCN recognition for MSI-H/dMMR and TMB-high; no LMS-specific recommendation

trials.title: Pembrolizumab in advanced solid tumours (KEYNOTE-158)
trials.indication: advanced solid tumours including TMB-high cohort
trials.notes: Closed to accrual. Cited as the basis for the tumour-agnostic TMB-high approval, not as an enrolment route.

manufacturer.notes: Phone from the current Keytruda FDA label.

payer_access_notes: MSI-high or TMB >= 10 mut/Mb on a validated tissue assay converts this from an off-label appeal into an on-label claim. The tumour-agnostic TMB indication also requires prior therapy, so it is a post-induction claim even if TMB comes back high.
next_steps: Include validated tissue TMB and MSI reporting in tissue order A, and MMR IHC in tissue order B. Both are cheap and both can open an on-label door.
If TMB >= 10 or MSI-high, revisit after the first chemotherapy line, since the agnostic indication requires prior therapy.
If both are negative, treat single-agent checkpoint blockade in uLMS as closed and put the effort into the antigen-directed branches instead.
Merck medical information: 1-877-888-4231.
geographic_scope: US-wide
notes: The tumour-agnostic route is post-induction by label design. The testing that determines whether the route exists at all should still happen now.

access_summary: Approved in many tumour types, so prescribable off-label, but the dedicated uterine leiomyosarcoma phase 2 was negative and there is no biomarker in this case pointing the other way. Access is easy; the reason not to pursue it is the evidence, not the route.
regulatory_status: FDA-approved across multiple solid tumours; no sarcoma indication.
payer_access_notes: Off-label single-agent PD-1 blockade in uLMS against a negative phase 2 will be denied and should be.
next_steps: No action. Recorded so the negative is visible rather than absent.
geographic_scope: US-wide

access_summary: Both drugs are approved and the combination is prescribable off-label. Alliance A091401 showed the combination beat single-agent nivolumab in sarcoma overall, but the leiomyosarcoma contribution was thin and the toxicity is not. This is a later-line consideration with a real off-label coverage fight attached.
regulatory_status: Both FDA-approved across multiple solid tumours; no sarcoma indication.
payer_access_notes: Dual checkpoint blockade off-label is expensive and will draw a full review. A091401 is the citation, but it is a randomised phase 2 without a sarcoma indication behind it.
next_steps: Defer to later lines.
If pursued, file with the A091401 data and an explicit toxicity-monitoring plan.
geographic_scope: US-wide

access_summary: Both components are approved, so a first-line doxorubicin plus pembrolizumab regimen is prescribable off-label, but the supporting data is a phase 1/2 and there is no trial in this dossier offering it on protocol. Compared with the planned LMS-04 regimen it trades a phase 3 result for a phase 2 one, which is the reason to be cautious rather than any access barrier.
regulatory_status: Doxorubicin generic; pembrolizumab FDA-approved in other indications. The combination has no sarcoma indication.
payer_access_notes: Off-label pembrolizumab first line in sarcoma without an MSI or TMB result is very unlikely to clear.
next_steps: Not a realistic first-line substitution for LMS-04 on access grounds.
If chemo-immunotherapy is genuinely wanted, the ivonescimab trial is the better-supported route to a PD-1 axis drug in this window.
geographic_scope: US-wide

access_summary: Jemperli carries a tumour-agnostic accelerated approval for mismatch-repair-deficient recurrent or advanced solid tumours after prior therapy. MMR has never been tested on her tissue. It is rarely positive in uLMS but the IHC is cheap, so close the question rather than assume it.
regulatory_status: FDA-approved for dMMR recurrent or advanced solid tumours that have progressed on prior treatment, and in dMMR/MSI-H endometrial cancer. No sarcoma-specific indication.

trials.title: Dostarlimab (TSR-042) in advanced solid tumours (GARNET)
trials.notes: Closed to accrual. The basis for the tumour-agnostic dMMR indication.

manufacturer.country_of_origin: United Kingdom; US operations Philadelphia, PA
manufacturer.notes: Phone from the current Jemperli FDA label.

payer_access_notes: With dMMR documented, this is an on-label claim after prior therapy. Without it there is nothing to file.
next_steps: Add MMR IHC (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6) to tissue order B; it rides the same block cut as INI1 and costs almost nothing extra.
If dMMR is found, this becomes a real post-induction option and GSK medical information at 1-888-825-5249 can supply the label package.
geographic_scope: US-wide, contingent on a dMMR result

access_summary: Tazverik is approved in epithelioid sarcoma, not uterine leiomyosarcoma, so every route here is off-label or trial-based cross-histology extrapolation. The gate is INI1 IHC on tumour tissue: a plasma SMARCB1 frameshift is a hypothesis, and no payer and no trial will act on it. Both tazemetostat expanded-access programs are listed as no longer available, so if INI1 loss is confirmed the realistic path is an off-label prescription with an appeal built on the INI1-negative basket data.
regulatory_status: FDA-approved (accelerated) for metastatic or locally advanced epithelioid sarcoma not eligible for complete resection in patients 16 and older, and for relapsed/refractory follicular lymphoma. Not approved in leiomyosarcoma.
guideline_status: NCCN recognition is in epithelioid sarcoma; off-guideline for uterine leiomyosarcoma

trials.title: Tazemetostat in adult participants with soft tissue sarcoma
trials.indication: INI1-negative and SWI/SNF-altered soft tissue sarcoma
trials.notes: Closed. The registration cohort plus the INI1-negative basket cohorts; the evidence to cite in an off-label appeal, not an enrolment route.

trials.title: Tazemetostat Expanded Access Program for adults with solid tumours
trials.indication: solid tumours on the sponsor's eligible-condition list
trials.notes: Listed on the registry as no longer available. Checked so the reader can see the expanded-access door was tried and is shut.

trials.title: Tazemetostat Expanded Access Program for adults with epithelioid sarcoma
trials.notes: Also no longer available, and epithelioid-sarcoma-only in any case.

manufacturer.notes: Phone taken verbatim from the current Tazverik FDA label: 'For more information, contact Epizyme at 855-463-5127.' No separate compassionate-use email was verifiable this run; ask the medical information line for the current managed-access route.

payer_access_notes: Off-label EZH2 inhibition in uLMS is expensive and will be reviewed carefully. A documented loss of nuclear INI1 staining, ideally on both the 2024 uterine block and the 2026 lung core, is what makes the appeal arguable. Without it there is no filing worth making.
next_steps: Order INI1/SMARCB1 IHC (BAF47 clone) on tumour tissue as part of tissue order B. That single stain decides whether this branch exists.
Order it on both the 2024 uterine block and the 2026 pulmonary core; discordance between primary and metastasis is a known problem and one negative on a small core is not reassuring.
If INI1 is lost, call Epizyme/Ipsen medical information at 855-463-5127 and ask what managed-access or named-patient route currently exists, since both registered expanded-access programs are closed.
In parallel, ask about NCT07303387 (valemetostat), which requires a bi-allelic homozygous deletion her plasma frameshift does not establish.
If INI1 is intact, close this branch and say so in the record rather than leaving it open.
geographic_scope: US-wide as an off-label prescription; no open expanded-access program
notes: The load-bearing honesty in this case: SMARCB1 loss is uncommon in uterine leiomyosarcoma, and the call came from plasma at unstated variant fraction. The prior is low, the confirmatory test is cheap, and the branch should not be priced as if it were already true.

access_summary: The trial route for the SWI/SNF branch is a Gustave Roussy basket study, and it is stricter than the tazemetostat data: it requires a documented bi-allelic homozygous deletion of SMARCB1 by validated NGS plus centrally confirmed loss of expression by IHC. A single plasma frameshift does not meet that. It is also France-only, four sites, with an ECOG 0-1 ceiling and a maximum of one prior treatment line in the SMARCB1 cohort.
regulatory_status: Approved in Japan (Ezharmia) for adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma and peripheral T-cell lymphoma. No FDA or EMA approval; investigational in solid tumours.

trials.title: Efficacy and safety of valemetostat in selected solid tumours
trials.notes: Four sites, all in France. Criterion 8 requires bi-allelic (homozygous) deletion by validated NGS and centrally confirmed loss of expression by IHC. Cohort 1.A allows a maximum of one prior treatment line, so if she enrolled it would have to be either now or immediately after induction. ECOG 0-1.

payer_access_notes: Not a payer question. Study drug is supplied on trial; the cost is travel and the screening biopsy work.
next_steps: Confirm a US or EU site is accepting international patients before anything else. As registered this is a France-only study and she is US-based.

Email Dr Postel-Vinay at SOPHIE.POSTEL-VINAY@gustaveroussy.fr to ask whether a truncating SMARCB1 frameshift with confirmed INI1 loss by IHC can substitute for a documented homozygous deletion. That single answer decides whether the trial is even theoretically open to her.
Order the tissue NGS and INI1 IHC now; both are prerequisites for any version of this conversation.
Note the one-prior-line cap: after LMS-04 induction she would still be within it, but only just.
geographic_scope: France only as registered; no US site
notes: A reader scanning the trial table sees a recruiting SMARCB1 study and assumes a door. The bi-allelic homozygous deletion requirement and the France-only geography are both hard, and her plasma frameshift satisfies neither.

Foghorn's FHD-609 and C4 Therapeutics' CFT8634 each ran phase 1 studies in synovial sarcoma and SMARCB1-null tumours and both closed without a successor program on the registry. There is no trial, no expanded access and no approved drug in this class.

Atezolizumab alone is approved and could be prescribed off-label, but single-agent PD-L1 blockade in uLMS has the same negative evidence base as the other checkpoint rows.

access_summary: SURPASS is the MAGE-A4 TCR-T study that admits tumour types beyond synovial sarcoma, and it is closed to accrual. It also carries the criterion that recurs across this whole class and matters most in her case: at least 90% room-air oxygen saturation at rest, measured at screening and again at baseline. At 8,500 ft a resting room-air saturation in the high 80s can be physiologically normal, and the cell-therapy protocols in this class write the criterion as an absolute number with no altitude clause. Get the oximetry done and recorded with the altitude noted, and raise the interpretation with the sponsor's medical monitor before screening rather than after a failed check.
regulatory_status: Investigational; no approval anywhere.

Document the ECOG; this protocol caps at 0-1.
Order MAGE-A4 IHC as part of tissue order C only if a MAGE-A4 program is actually open to her.

Ask about resting room-air oxygen saturation requirements and flag the 8,500 ft residence in that first message.

That makes it reachable now, before LMS-04, and it is the only investigational option in the dossier where declining induction is written into the protocol rather than argued around it. Patients who decline the standard of care first-line systemic therapy will be eligible for this trial.' ECOG 0-2. access_summary: The one live US ATR seat. The NCI dose-escalation arm admits extracranial solid tumours where temozolomide is guideline-standard, which covers soft-tissue sarcoma without requiring an MGMT result, and the ECOG ceiling is 2. It requires progression on, intolerance of, or refusal of available therapies, so in practice it opens after LMS-04. Two sequencing traps sit upstream: prior temozolomide is disqualifying, so an off-label olaparib plus temozolomide line would close this door, and the ATR-for-ALT rationale should be priced as unproven in her histology, because the ATRX-mutant leiomyosarcoma monotherapy cohort progressed within 4 months despite biopsy-proven target engagement.

If her tissue NGS returns ATRX loss, this study's read-out becomes the nearest future test of whether that selection logic works in anyone.

access_summary: Supersedes the earlier access row for this intervention, adding the eligibility gate that row missed: entry requires intact Rb expression by immunohistochemistry on the baseline biopsy or archived tumour, assessed at MD Anderson with a CLIA-certified antibody. That is the exact opposite gate from the RB1-negative CDK7 protocol at the same institution, so one Rb stain on the tissue-order-B block routes her between the two trials: Rb intact points here, Rb lost points to REC-617 after a first line. The first-line opening stands, and so does the trap: the phase 2 portion admits systemic-treatment-naive patients, prior gemcitabine is disqualifying, and the ECOG ceiling is 2.
regulatory_status: Abemaciclib (Verzenio) FDA-approved in HR-positive HER2-negative breast cancer. No sarcoma indication. Gemcitabine and docetaxel are generic.
